originalTitle: India to be key player in AI and biotechnology - led industrial revolution : MoS
content:
New Delhi, Aug 9 : India is poised to become a major force in the next industrial revolution, which will be driven by artificial intelligence and biotechnology, Union Minister of State Dr Jitendra Singh said on Sunday.

He said the country has positioned itself among the world's early movers in emerging technologies through initiatives such as the BioE3 policy, National Quantum Mission and IndiaAI Mission.

Addressing a media conclave attended by technology developers, industry leaders and other stakeholders, Singh said India has emerged as one of the first countries to formulate a dedicated biotechnology policy, BioE3 (Biotechnology for Economy, Employment and Environment), while also launching initiatives such as the National Quantum Mission and the IndiaAI Mission.

"India will be an essential player in the next industrial revolution which will be biotechnology and AI driven, unlike the last industrial revolution which was IT driven and India was late in becoming a part of that," Singh stated.

"India is now among the first few countries in the world to have a dedicated Biotechnology policy, that is BiOE3," the minister said.

The minister said the global economy is gradually shifting towards frontier sectors including biotechnology, artificial intelligence, recycling and the circular economy, and India is positioning itself at the forefront of this transition.

Unlike the previous industrial revolution that was largely driven by information technology, where India joined the global transformation at a later stage, the country is now among the early participants shaping the next wave of innovation, he said.

Highlighting India's rapid technological progress, Singh said the country's space economy, which was once negligible in size, has grown to around $9 billion and is projected to reach $40-45 billion over the next eight to nine years.

He attributed this growth to policy reforms, particularly the decision to open the space sector to private participation in 2020.

"India's technological journey has undergone a significant transformation, with the country now operating against global benchmarks in several areas," Singh mentioned.
chineseTitle: 印度将成为 AI 和生物技术主导的工业革命的关键参与者：MoS
chineseContent:
新德里，8 月 9 日：印度联邦国务部长 Jitendra Singh 博士周日表示，印度将成为下一次工业革命的主要力量，这次工业革命将由人工智能和生物技术推动。

他表示，通过 BioE3 政策、国家量子任务和 IndiaAI Mission 等举措，印度已将自己定位为世界新兴技术的先行者之一。

辛格在技术开发商、行业领袖和其他利益相关者出席的媒体会议上发表讲话时表示，印度已成为最早制定专门生物技术政策 BioE3（生物技术促进经济、就业和环境）的国家之一，同时还发起了国家量子任务和 IndiaAI 任务等举措。

辛格表示：“印度将成为下一次工业革命的重要参与者，这次工业革命将由生物技术和人工智能驱动，而上一次工业革命是由信息技术驱动的，而印度很晚才成为其中的一部分。”

“印度现在是世界上最早制定专门生物技术政策（BiOE3）的几个国家之一，”该部长说。

这位部长表示，全球经济正在逐渐转向生物技术、人工智能、回收和循环经济等前沿领域，而印度正处于这一转型的最前沿。

他说，与之前主要由信息技术推动的工业革命不同，印度是在较晚阶段才加入全球转型的，而印度现在是塑造下一波创新浪潮的早期参与者之一。

辛格强调了印度快速的技术进步，表示该国的航天经济规模曾经可以忽略不计，现已增长到约 90 亿美元，预计在未来 8 至 9 年内将达到 40 至 450 亿美元。

他将这一增长归因于政策改革，特别是 2020 年向私人参与开放航天领域的决定。

辛格表示：“印度的技术之旅已经发生了重大转变，该国目前在多个领域都在按照全球基准进行运营。”
